A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FARE research and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish reliable correspondence throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original FARE training and evaluation results, including benchmark performance, downstream applications, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds comparator results in Figure 4 and Table 9.

M1.justification: The FARE models, iterative rejection-sampling SFT procedure, direct-judgment training, continuous curriculum, and inference prompts remain unchanged. The added verifiers and judges are comparison methods, not changes to FARE.

E1.justification: Training data, five evaluation tasks, core benchmarks, and downstream scenarios are unchanged, including supplementary evaluations in Appendix D. The additions evaluate more comparators within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds General-Verifier to the GRPO verifier comparison. Table 9 adds GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o to the general-purpose model comparison; GPT-4o already appeared in other experiments in v1. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same reported metrics, evaluation procedures, reranking setup, and GRPO training settings. No split, budget, or protocol revision accompanies the added comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same direct-judgment, curriculum, and CoT ablations, positional-bias analysis, and JETTS prompt comparisons. The added benchmark comparators introduce no distinct robustness or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The added comparator results use point estimates without introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 4 newly reports General-Verifier's average of 41.3, versus unchanged FARE-8B/20B averages of 43.1/45.2; Section 4.2 adds relative advantages of 4.4%/9.4%. Table 9 adds GPT-4.1/GPT-4o results, including JudgeBench scores of 66.29/50.29. Retained numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The evaluator formalization, SFT objective in Equation 1, and mathematical descriptions of training and rewards are unchanged. No definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about large-scale multi-task training, FARE performance, and three downstream applications. The new comparisons support existing claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning RL convergence, cross-domain verification, CoT effects, and positional robustness remain unchanged, as do appendix discussions of reranking failures. The added comparator evidence introduces no new mechanism explanation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, hyperparameters, data-processing details, and prompts in Appendices B, C, and E are unchanged. No new implementation recipe or code/data access information accompanies the added baselines.

R1.justification: Section 4.2 modestly extends positioning against Ma et al. (2025): alongside the existing General-Reasoner comparison, v2 directly compares with General-Verifier and emphasizes its in-distribution verification training. The bibliography and dedicated related-work sections remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the verifier-comparison prose and Figure 4 caption, replacement of 'Our model' labels with FARE names in Table 9, and the version/date stamp. Section organization and the wider narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains a General-Verifier bar series and legend entry, while Table 9 gains two rows. Nearby figures, tables, and prose shift slightly, but there is no substantial visual redesign or reorganization.

improvement.justification: The added trained-verifier comparison in Figure 4 strengthens evidence for FARE's usefulness during RL beyond comparison with string matching. GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o results in Table 9 provide additional reference points. These are useful, limited improvements to comparative support; the method, existing FARE results, and analytical depth remain stable.
